title: ramp-to-sla-30min-dev-econ-notes
summary: Working brief: developer-first hosted API positioning with microcopy, 30m quickstart flow, and pricing phrasing experiments focused on reducing time-to-value and clarifying unit economics for engineers.
content:
Objective:
- Create a compact, developer-first message kit for the Hosted API that drives fast integration (30m -> SLA trial) and sets clear expectations on cost.
- Produce short microcopy variants for CTAs, email snippets, and CLI/cURL quickstarts.
- Draft pricing language that engineers / platform teams trust (transparent, deterministic, measurable).

Context / problem statements (notes to self):
- Developers abandon trials when token cost is opaque or the first demo costs >$5 unexpectedly. Need clear upfront anchors.
- Engineering buyers care about performance predictability (p99 latency, token price, retry behavior); marketing often defaults to feature lists.
- Competitors emphasize model breadth or low per-token prices but hide batching/latency tradeoffs. Our angle should be: predictable unit economics + dev ergonomics for production.

Key developer-first value props (short lines to use in headers / cards):
1) "Integrate in minutes. Predict costs by design."
2) "Same API from sandbox to SLA-backed production."
3) "Token billing that maps to real engineering tradeoffs — you choose speed, cost, and reliability."
4) "Built-in fallbacks and autoscaling for production traffic spikes."
5) "Developer-friendly SDKs, streaming, and examples that work in your stack."

Supporting bullets (use in feature sections / expansion):
- Quickstart: Hello world in 30s, sample app to SLA in 30 minutes (template for Node/Python/Rust).
- Observability: per-route latency & cost breakdowns; token-level tracing hooks.
- Controls: batch size & cache policies exposed; recommended profiles for chat vs. single-shot generation.
- Safety & enterprise: VPC options, audit logs, and dedicated capacity for regulated data.

30m quickstart play (micro flow we can show on a single page):
- 0–1m: Create account, copy API key (CTA copy: "Get API key — start free" / alt: "Create key (no credit card)").
- 1–3m: Run example curl or SDK snippet: obtain a streaming response in 2 lines.
  Example cURL microcopy: "curl -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-small\",\"prompt\":\"Hello\"}'"
- 3–10m: Run Quickstart app (repo link) — README has "30m: deploy sample to your cloud and hit /chat".
- 10–25m: Swap in your model config (latency budget, batching policy) and run a small load test.
- 25–30m: Look at Console -> Route metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens, cost) and enable trial SLA or reserve a small Dedicated pool.

Microcopy variants (A/B test ideas):
- CTA A: "Try live — 30s setup"
- CTA B: "Hello world in under a minute"
- Pricing headline A: "Pay per token — exact math, no surprises"
- Pricing headline B: "Clear unit pricing, optimized by workload"

Pricing-language drafts (engineer-targeted):
- Long form (docs): "Tokens billed per input+output token. Cost per 1k tokens is model-specific; our Console shows the effective cost per API call after batching and caching. Use per-route profiles to control throughput vs. unit price."
- Short form (UI): "Tokens billed. See predicted cost for your request in the SDK and Console."
- Email snippet: "Starter tier includes 10k free tokens. Predictable pay-as-you-go thereafter; upgrade to Dedicated for flat monthly capacity and committed unit pricing."

Pricing framing & decision rules we should test:
- Show "estimated cost" before first request based on sample inputs (reduces fear of surprise charges).
- Surface "expected latency" for chosen model + batching profile.
- Offer a small reserved pool trial (1–2 GPUs) with a simple toggle in Console to let engineers see flat unit economics.

Competitive analysis notes (quick, opinionated):
- Major cloud AI providers: good for multi-model catalogs and billing familiarity, but often opaque batching layers and poor dev UX for streaming + fast iteration.
- LLM API-first competitors: emphasize simplicity; however, they trade off production predictability (limited control over batching/caching) — our messaging: "control, not complexity."
- Self-host runtimes: cheapest at scale but high ops burden; position Redwood as "the best-of-both" — managed offering with production knobs and optional Dedicated/Private deployments.

Risks & open questions (to follow-up):
- Does legal want a specific phrasing around "free tokens" and credit cards? (ask finance/legal: FIN-24-apply)
- How accurate are our Console "estimated cost" projections for short prompts? Need engineering signoff and a tolerance band.
- Rolling out reserved-pool trials: what SLAs do we expose for 7-day trials? Ops input required.

Sample short messaging blocks (for landing page / email):
- Hero: "Ship LLM features that meet your latency and budget goals"
- Sub-hero: "Integrate in minutes. Measure costs per route. Scale with controls that map to engineering tradeoffs."
- Feature bullets: "30s hello world", "Token-cost preview", "Canary rollouts + automatic fallback"

Callout: "Predictable Economics" (1-paragraph explainer we can use as tooltip):
- "Real-world LLM costs depend on throughput patterns, request shapes, and caching. Redwood exposes the knobs (batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles) and shows the downstream impact on cost and latency so engineering teams can make deterministic tradeoffs without guesswork."

Examples of objection-handling lines for sales/SEs:
- Q: "Why is your price higher than competitor X?"
  A: "Our per-call latency and production SLAs factor into the unit economics; with our batching and caching controls you'll often see lower effective cost for interactive apps. If you have steady throughput we can recommend a Dedicated profile with committed pricing."
- Q: "Can I estimate cost for my workload?"
  A: "Yes — use our Quickstart + Console to simulate 1k requests and get a modeled cost and latency distribution. We also offer consulting for larger pilots."

Metrics and success criteria for the play (what to measure):
- Activation: % of signups that run first successful generate call within 30 minutes (target: 35% -> 50% after copy tweaks).
- Cost shock: % of customers who exceed $5 spend in first session (target <5%).
- Conversion to paid (30d): from trial with Reserved pool enabled -> 12%.
- Time-to-SLA: median time from signup to enabling trial SLA (target: <2 days).

Experiment matrix (suggested A/Bs):
1) CTA phrasing: "30s setup" vs "Hello world in under a minute"
2) Pricing anchor: show "estimated cost before first call" vs hide it
3) Starter offer: 10k free tokens vs 2k free tokens + 1-day reserved pool trial
4) Quickstart type: web-in-AWS template vs local CLI-first template

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Engineering: provide example cURL + Node/Python snippet and add cost estimate API (owner: Devon).
- [ ] Growth: wire landing page A/B with CTA variants (owner: Sofia).
- [ ] Legal/Finance: approve language for "free tokens" and trial reserved pools (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Product: define reserved-pool trial SLA and billing mechanism (owner: Asha).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep microcopy short, avoid marketing fluff (engineers skim).
- Inline code snippets should be copy-paste ready; test on mac/linux shells.
- Avoid overpromising latency numbers — show distributions (p50/p95/p99).

Possible future additions (nice-to-have):
- Small interactive cost simulator widget that takes example prompts and returns estimated tokens + cost.
- Pre-built per-language sample apps (React, Next.js, Flask, FastAPI) that show Console metrics wired in.

End — this is an intentionally compact brief to iterate quickly. Fill in SDK snippets and Console screenshots in the next draft.

Feedback welcome: add comments inline or ping me on #gtm-hosted-api.
